title: Lockit Cartographer — bilingual gettext bundle
description: The NORMATIVE contract for the BILINGUAL profile emitted by lockit-cartographer. A bundle is a directory holding exactly two files: lines.jsonl (one row object per line, UTF-8, LF, no BOM, exactly one trailing newline) and manifest.json (one manifest object). This file describes the bilingual gettext profile ONLY. It does NOT describe the span-oriented monolingual profile that scripts/veloren/export_bundle.py emits against a different consumer's contracts; the two are different contracts by design and must never be merged. This repository is the producer and owns this file; a consumer's copy is a validating mirror, and a divergence between them is a bug owned by whoever let the mirror drift. STANDING RULE: whoever rewrites lines.jsonl rewrites manifest.json in the same act. A row file that has moved while the manifest's content_hash has not is the one corruption nothing else in the chain can detect. lines.jsonl is therefore always written BEFORE manifest.json, so a torn run leaves a bundle with no manifest (rejected on sight) rather than a manifest asserting a hash for bytes that are not there.

manifest.description: manifest.json — one object describing the whole bundle.

bundle_version.description: Version of THIS CONTRACT — the bilingual gettext profile this file describes — and NOT of the bundle instance and NOT of the producer. Pinned with const on purpose: an unconstrained version token lets two bundles that mean different things by the same token validate identically, which is exactly what happened in this repository already — scripts/veloren/export_bundle.py shipped 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 bundles that no validator could tell apart, and the version string was the only discriminator a consumer had. With const, a consumer holding a mirror of 1.0.0 rejects a 2.0.0 bundle loudly at validation time instead of reading it as though nothing had changed. cartographer_version is a DIFFERENT thing: it versions the producing exporter, and one producer version can ship two contracts just as easily as one contract can ship from two producer versions. The 0.2.0 / 0.3.0 numbering used by this repository's Veloren exporter belongs to a DIFFERENT consumer's contract — an unrelated series that this one deliberately does not continue, so do not assume a single numbering across this repository. BUMP RULE: a change a conforming consumer can ignore is a minor bump, and any change to the field list, to a field's type, or to a field's meaning is a major bump.

game.description: Stable slug of the game / dataset this lockit belongs to, e.g. "battle-for-wesnoth".

source_format.description: The native lockit format the rows were read from. This profile is gettext only; another format gets its own contract, not a widened enum.

source_locale.description: BCP-47-ish tag of the source side, matching lines[].source_en. "en" for Wesnoth.

target_locale.description: BCP-47-ish tag of the target side, matching lines[].target_pl.

upstream.description: Provenance of the TREE the .po files were read from. All four are required and none may be fabricated: a bundle whose upstream cannot be established must not be written at all.

remote.description: The upstream git remote URL, read from the checkout's .git/config.

commit.description: Full 40-hex commit of the checkout the rows were read from.

branch.description: The branch the checkout is on.

po_revision_dates.description: MAP, textdomain -> the PO-Revision-Date string from that domain's target .po header, verbatim. This is the ONE object in this schema that is not closed: its keys are exactly the bundle's textdomains[], which are data and cannot be listed in a schema written in advance. It is typed as a string map rather than left open, and no second exception exists anywhere in this file. A domain whose header carries no PO-Revision-Date is present with an empty string, never absent.

extraction_script_hash.description: sha256 over the CONCATENATED BYTES of the exporter script AND every first-party module it imports, in ascending byte order of their repository-relative POSIX paths. Hashing the exporter alone would pin one file and leave the PO parser free to move underneath it, which is the change most likely to alter what a row says while the exporter's own bytes stay put. The producer reports the exact file list with every export.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the payload bytes of lines.jsonl EXACTLY AS WRITTEN — not over a re-serialisation of the parsed rows, which would hide a text-mode write, a BOM, or CRLF. Verifying it is a byte read plus one digest, which is what makes 'the rows moved and the manifest did not' detectable at all.

value.description: 64 lowercase hex characters, no algorithm prefix.

line_count.description: Number of row objects in lines.jsonl. Must equal the actual line count.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant the bundle was produced (…Z, second precision). This is the only manifest field that differs between two runs over identical input; it is deliberately NOT covered by content_hash, so payload reproducibility can still be asserted byte-for-byte.

cartographer_version.description: Version of the producing exporter. Bump it whenever a change would move content_hash for unchanged input.

textdomains.description: Byte-sorted union of the textdomains in the SOURCE (.pot) corpus — the full inventory, not only the domains that produced rows. A domain present upstream but missing on the target side is still listed here, and is named in the producer's report rather than silently dropped or counted as zero.

line.description: One row of lines.jsonl = one gettext entry. A plural entry is ONE row, never several. Every property below is required and always present; a value that does not apply is null, never absent and never an empty string.

segment_id.description: Stable join key across exports. EXACT PREIMAGE, reproduce it verbatim or your ids will not join: textdomain + ":" + sha1( ((msgctxt or "") + "|" + msgid_raw).encode("utf-8") ).hexdigest()[:12], lowercase. It is a pure function of (textdomain, msgctxt, msgid_raw) and NOTHING else — not seq, not file, not line number, not msgid_plural, and not the unescaped display form of the text. msgid_raw is the msgid with PO escapes intact (a newline is the two characters backslash-n), including any Wesnoth ^-context prefix. HAZARD, recorded and deliberately not fixed: the separator is a literal "|", and "|" occurs inside Wesnoth source text as the documented $var| terminator. The preimage is injective here only because msgctxt is empty on every Wesnoth entry, so nothing can straddle the separator. For the NEXT lockit — one that actually uses msgctxt — this construction is NOT injective and must be revisited before it is reused. NOTE: this is a different function from the 10-character internal_id that the Cartographer's PO reader mints for its own use (that one hashes domain and plural into the preimage with a 0x1f separator). They are the same shape and different values; joining on the wrong one produces a bundle that validates and matches nothing.

seq.description: 0-based, dense, global across the bundle. Export order is: textdomains byte-sorted (NOT locale-sorted), then entry order within the file.

textdomain.description: The gettext textdomain, i.e. the first half of segment_id.

file.description: Path of the target .po the row was read from, relative to the corpus root, forward slashes.

msgctxt.description: The disambiguating context, or null. For gettext lockits that use msgctxt this is that field verbatim. For Wesnoth it is DERIVED: Wesnoth disambiguates with a ^-prefix inside the msgid rather than with msgctxt, so the caret prefix is surfaced here as the native disambiguator. source_en still carries the WHOLE raw msgid including the prefix, because the id is computed over that. Leaving this null would discard the gender/agreement prefix family, which is the most translation-critical signal in this corpus for a Slavic target.

source_en.description: NORMATIVE source text: the RAW msgid, PO escapes intact, exactly as the foundation reader returns it, whitespace untouched. The id is computed over this, and any future character offset anchors here.

source_en_display.description: DERIVED and NON-NORMATIVE: source_en with PO escapes resolved to real characters. Exists so a consumer can hand natural prose to a model without the producer having to guess which form it wants. Never an input to placeholder or markup detection — those run on the raw form, because that is what the detectors are written against.

target_pl.description: NORMATIVE target text: the RAW msgstr (msgstr[0] for a plural entry), escapes intact. null when the target is empty — never the empty string. A fuzzy entry keeps its text here; see pool and fuzzy.

target_pl_display.description: DERIVED and NON-NORMATIVE unescaped form of target_pl. null EXACTLY when target_pl is null.

fuzzy.description: The gettext #, fuzzy flag. Kept as its own boolean so the distinction survives pool collapsing fuzzy into untranslated.

plural_forms.description: null for a non-plural entry. For a plural entry, an object carrying BOTH sides — the earlier array-of-strings shape could not say which side a string belonged to. source_en stays the singular msgid and target_pl stays msgstr[0], so a consumer that ignores plurals entirely still reads a coherent bilingual pair and never a broken row.

target_forms.description: Every msgstr[N] in index order, RAW. May contain empty strings for a partially filled plural; that is data, not an error.

target_forms_display.description: Unescaped mirror of target_forms, same length. Derived, non-normative.

target_nplurals.description: nplurals from the target .po header's Plural-Forms, NOT the length of target_forms. When the array length disagrees with the header that is a REPORTED number, never a silent fix — the header is what the runtime uses, so the array is the thing that is wrong.

placeholders.description: Plain string tokens found in the RAW source_en: Wesnoth $var / $obj.attr / $arr[0] (the trailing | terminator normalised away, so $x and $x| are one token), {brace} name-generator keys, and printf specifiers. Sorted, deduplicated. DELIBERATELY NOT SPANS: character offsets are strictly more informative and are what the span-oriented consumer's profile wants, but this profile's schema is closed and would reject them. A consumer that needs spans takes the span profile, not this one.

markup_flags.description: Which markup systems the RAW source_en carries, from the producer's markup family detection. Closed vocabulary. Sorted, deduplicated, possibly empty.

string_class.description: "<domain-group>/<caret-family>", or "unknown" when neither resolves. Deliberately NOT the bare textdomain: a consumer reading string_class "wesnoth-lib" gets a value that validates and carries no meaning. The domain group comes from the profiled anatomy (ui, core, units, campaign, help, manpages, tutorial, mp_editor, tools); the caret family from the ^-context prefix registry, with "plain" for an entry that has no caret prefix.

neighbours.description: The previous and next segment_id in export order WITHIN THE SAME FILE. null at a file boundary — neighbours never cross textdomains, because adjacency across two unrelated domains is not context.

char_limit.description: Hard display length budget, when the lockit declares one. gettext has no such field, so this is null for every gettext row; the field is kept so a lockit that does declare limits can fill it without a schema change.

last_changed.description: When the row's .po file last changed upstream, ISO-8601, or null when it cannot be established cheaply and honestly. A shallow or grafted checkout reports the same date for every file, which is not an answer — null is.

pool.description: Which pool the row belongs to. Owned by the EXPORT, not by a downstream slicing step. untranslated when the target is empty AND when the entry is fuzzy (gettext does not use fuzzy strings at runtime, so fuzzy is not done); eval otherwise. "reference" is never written by an export — only a later curation step assigns it.

placeholder_check.description: Cross-locale placeholder agreement, computed as sets over the source tokens and the union of tokens across all target forms. ok: the sets are equal. source_only: the target dropped one or more source tokens and invented none. target_only: the target invented one or more tokens and dropped none. mismatch: both. not_applicable: the row is untranslated, or neither side carries a placeholder. THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING AND NOT A REFUSAL: a mismatched placeholder is a real upstream translation bug that has often been in a locale for years, and an exporter that refuses on it declines to export a corpus that legitimately contains it. The field exists so a curation step can either exclude such rows or include them deliberately labelled as known-bad reference cases, which it cannot do if the export threw the finding away.

source_ref.description: The gettext #: source references for this entry ("path/to/file.cpp:123"), verbatim and in file order, or null when the entry carries none. Provenance into the GAME's source, not into the lockit — the lockit location is `file` plus export order.
